source: Jim Rohn — Never Worry About Money Again (70/10/10/10 Formula)

rich_vs_poor_philosophy.name: Rich vs Poor Philosophy of Money
rich_vs_poor_philosophy.when: When discussing the foundational mindset of wealth building
rich_vs_poor_philosophy.poor_philosophy: Spend your money and invest what is left
rich_vs_poor_philosophy.rich_philosophy: Invest your money and spend what is left
rich_vs_poor_philosophy.insight: The amount does not matter. What matters is the philosophy. A child with a dollar can learn the same principle as an adult with a million.

seventy_ten_ten_ten.name: 70/10/10/10 Formula for Financial Independence
seventy_ten_ten_ten.when: When giving practical money management advice or teaching financial literacy

formula.seventy: Do not spend more than 70 cents of every dollar. This is your living expense cap.
formula.ten_charity: 10 cents for charity. Give to help people who cannot help themselves. Generosity builds character better than any class or book.
formula.ten_active: 10 cents as active capital. Invest in projects to make a profit. Wages make you a living but profits make you a fortune.
formula.ten_passive: 10 cents as passive capital. Let a financial institution use it. They pay you interest. This is where compound interest creates financial independence.

seventy_ten_ten_ten.key_insight: The borrower is servant to the lender. The power position is the lender, not the spender. Build toward being a lender.

profits_over_wages.name: Profits Over Wages
profits_over_wages.when: When discussing why entrepreneurship or side income matters
profits_over_wages.essence: Wages make you a living. Profits make you a fortune. There is no limit to profits. They can double, triple, and quadruple. Wages are capped. Profits are not.
profits_over_wages.example: Find a broken wagon for $1, fix it up, sell it for $5. Anybody can do that. Find something, touch it, make it better, make a profit. Society now has a mended wagon.

compound_interest_independence.name: Compound Interest Path to Independence
compound_interest_independence.when: When explaining how passive income works or why saving early matters
compound_interest_independence.essence: Passive capital = letting someone else use your money. They make a profit, pay you interest. Over time compound interest makes you financially independent.
compound_interest_independence.result: You will have the ability to live from the income of your own resources. That is the definition of financial independence.

attitude_tax_bills.name: The Attitude Advantage on Bills and Taxes
attitude_tax_bills.when: When addressing resistance to financial responsibilities
reframe: Bills: You are not 'paying bills' — you are reducing liabilities and increasing assets. Love that.
Taxes: You are caring for the goose that lays the golden eggs. Gladly pay your share while working to lower them.
attitude_tax_bills.essence: Same action, different frame. The frame determines whether you feel resentment or empowerment.

four_questions_to_ponder.name: Four Questions to Ponder
four_questions_to_ponder.when: When motivating someone to take action on their goals or self-development

questions.meaning: Why work this hard? Why take classes? Why read books? Why do the disciplines?
Why not see how many skills you can develop? How valuable you can become? How far you can go?
If others can read, change, figure it out, turn it around — why not you?
What better time than now to set goals, develop skills, get it together?

four_questions_to_ponder.use: Use these four questions in sequence to move someone from resistance to action.

key_tactics: The amount does not matter. The philosophy of what you do with it matters.
Invest first, spend what is left. Not the reverse.
70% max on living expenses. 10% charity. 10% active capital. 10% passive capital.
Wages make a living. Profits make a fortune. Prioritize profit-generating activity.
Compound interest through passive capital is the path to living from your own resources.
Be a lender not a borrower. That is the power position.
Reframe bills as liability reduction. Reframe taxes as feeding the goose.
Four-question sequence: Why → Why not → Why not you → Why not now.
